extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in freethought, secular ethics, and late-19th-century intellectual autobiography
extracted.subtask_description: Long-form autobiographical/argumentative essay explaining the author's atheism and outlining a secular basis for morality, social reform, and ideals of human development. Mixes personal narrative, philosophical argument, and prescriptive claims about ethics and social policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: True basis of morality — utility
rubrics_metrics.description: "The true basis of morality is utility; that is, the adaptation of our actions to the promotion of the general welfare and happiness; the endeavour so to rule our lives that we may serve and bless mankind."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morality should be founded on observable consequences and the promotion of general welfare rather than revelation or intuition. The essay argues that "virtue is an indispensable part of all true and solid happiness" and that obedience to law (natural/social) results in harmony and happiness. This is advanced as a basis acceptable to both thoughtful students and artisans, and as one that will keep morality separate from theological disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not remove old moral sanctions until replacements are ready
rubrics_metrics.description: "It therefore becomes the duty of every one who fights in the ranks of Freethought... to beware how he uproots sanctions of morality which he is too weak to replace, or how, before he is prepared with better ones, he removes the barriers which do yet, however poorly, to some extent check vice and repress crime."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When challenging religious doctrines that undergird social morality, activists must ensure alternative moral supports are established; otherwise, removing existing sanctions risks social harm. This functions as a procedural/ethical caution in reformist practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morality should be independent of theology
rubrics_metrics.description: Morality must be founded on a basis apart from theology so that it does not stand or totter with varying theories of the Divine nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author urges concentrating on 'attainable' study of phenomena and consequences to found morality in a way that endures beyond religious disputes. This includes using the study of facts and deduced laws to justify moral claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue is its own reward — intrinsic motivation for right conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: "Virtue was its own reward" and that payment on the other side of the grave is unnecessary as an incentive to right living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay contrasts two kinds of moral motive: selfish/calculating virtue (motivated by expected afterlife reward) and genuine virtue (motivated by love of right, service to others, and the intrinsic satisfaction of doing good). It rejects reliance on promises of immortality as the primary incentive for moral behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atheistic ideal of humanity — strong, free, socially-minded person
rubrics_metrics.description: The Atheist's ideal humanity is "in form strong and fair, perfect in physical development... radiant with love, glorious in self-reliant power... proud, true-hearted, loyal, brave" — a free man who brooks no tyranny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets an evaluative standard for human character and social ideals to inspire action: exalt physical and moral strength, self-reliance, fraternity, and active engagement in social improvement, contrasted with the Christian ideal of meekness and submissiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral growth needs an Ideal plus understanding of evils and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: To the forwarding of moral growth two things seemed necessary — an Ideal which should stir the emotions and impel to action, and a clear understanding of the sources of evil and of the methods by which they might be drained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical leadership must combine passionate inspirational imagery (the Ideal) with rigorous analysis of causes of wrongdoing and concrete methods (education, social reform) to remove them. Both elements are required; one without the other is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evil primarily arises from ignorance and adverse circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Evil comes from ignorance... parents who dwell in filthy, unventilated houses... live on insufficient food... bring into the world ill-nurtured children... from the sowing of misery, filth, and starvation shall arise crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explanatory standard for diagnosing social ills: emphasize environmental, economic, and educational causes (poverty, ignorance, poor housing, malnutrition) and prescribe remedies such as education and fair wages as the primary means to reduce crime and vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and personal improvement as cooperative with evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The knowledge that the perfecting of the race is only possible by the improvement of the individual supplies the most constraining motive for efforts after personal perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual moral improvement is framed as a social duty because each person's progress benefits the whole. This endorses personal purity and nobility as active contributions to evolutionary/social progress, not merely private goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolutionary account of conscience and social instincts
rubrics_metrics.description: The study of Darwin and Herbert Spencer... led me to see in the evolution of the social instinct the explanation of the growth of conscience and of the strengthening of man's mental and moral nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conscience and moral sentiments are to be understood as evolved social instincts; this grounds ethical development in naturalistic, scientific explanation and supports secular social policy interventions aimed at strengthening pro-social instincts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize attainable knowledge and experiment over unverifiable metaphysics
rubrics_metrics.description: Surely, then, we should do wisely to concentrate our strength and our energies on the discovery of the attainable, instead of on the search after the unknowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epistemic standard: prefer experimental, evidence-based inquiry (biology, chemistry, social science) for explaining life and guiding ethics rather than speculative metaphysics about souls or divine purpose. Belief should follow evidence: "For many of us evidence must precede belief."

rubrics_metrics.name: Prayer reinterpreted as contemplation and work
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is only one kind of prayer which is reasonable, and that is the deep, silent adoration of the greatness and beauty and order around us... The other part of prayer is work; from contemplation to labour, from the forest to the street."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spiritual practices are reframed as secular contemplation of ideals and active labour in the world; reverence and ethical action together constitute proper devotional life for the secular moralist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution against equating atheism with immorality — defend secular virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: The antagonism... regarded Atheism as implying degraded morality and bestial life, and they assailed my conduct not on evidence that it was evil, but on the presumption that an Atheist must be immoral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functions as both a rebuttal and evaluative principle: moral character must be judged by conduct and social contribution, not by theistic belief. The essay repeatedly defends that freethought produces self-reliant, altruistic motives and active commitment to social reform.
